rv.q: This production of “Cock” is truly special—not only for its flawless execution, but also its incredibly intimate presentation.
This visceral production is fast-paced, emotionally haunting, filled with anguish, and about changing partners and continuing “the dance.”

Altogether, this play is a confusing mess of newfound feelings and new levels of queerness, and for the emotional breadth that's covered, its rate of jokes-per-minute will leave you catching your breath between laughs.
This fine ensemble comes as close as they possibly can to doing so.
But antiquated conceptions of monogamy, marriage, antipathy in relationships, and sexuality bog down this production, as do the British colloquialisms.
Though not as scandalous as its title might imply, COCK is still an engaging, well-crafted work.

cn.t: Critics praise this intimate production of Bartlett's provocative drama about sexual fluidity and relationship dysfunction, with most finding it a well-crafted, emotionally charged "cockfight" that remains relevant despite its 2009 debut.
